copy.blurb:
The model fancies Australia more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against United States. +10.7pp is a wide disagreement by the engine's standards; that's what fires this as a Pick on the away side.

Public Elo rates United States 70 points higher than the other side (United States 1810, Australia 1740). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: United States to win at 44%, the draw at 26%, and Australia to win at 30%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Australia sits at 30% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: United States to win at 56%, the draw at 22%, and Australia to win at 19%. Kalshi has Australia at 19%, which prices out at American odds of +426; the model has the same side at 30%. The +10.7pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Australia, that haircut lands the model at 24%; the market is at 19%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +5.3pp. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 28 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Australia a stronger prior than the Kalshi line implies.
The +10.7pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The model thinks Australia are mispriced. Our number reads 30% on the away side; the market reads 19%. The +10.7pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: United States v Australia · the model leans Australia
